post_text:
Database migrations during zero-downtime deployments will break your JVM application if you do not decouple code releases from schema updates.

We learned this the hard way when a renamed database column instantly crashed active production instances.

Phase your changes using the Expand/Contract pattern to support two code versions simultaneously. Add nullable columns first, migrate data in the background, and only drop old fields after legacy JVM instances terminate. 🚀

Never run automated migration tools like Flyway directly inside your application startup path during horizontal scaling.

Multiple JVM nodes competing to lock the schema history table will cause startup deadlocks and cascade into deployment failures.

Enforce strict backward compatibility in your JPA entity mappings by explicitly ignoring unknown database columns.

This prevents your JVM classpath from throwing deserialization errors when the database schema evolves ahead of your application deployment.
lesson_extracted: Decouple database schema changes from application deployments using multi-phase migrations to prevent JVM startup deadlocks and runtime crashes.
